title: Universal syntax highlighter / OpaqueRange (demo)
brief: Demo of a universal syntax highlighter built on the new OpaqueRange web API (Chrome 152+, 2026) — syntax-highlighting different program fragments efficiently. Worth a look for anyone building code-rendering UI.
details: A demo from Sébastien Lorber of a universal syntax highlighter built on the OpaqueRange web API (new in Chrome 152, 2026) — a way to syntax-highlight different program fragments efficiently by styling ranges the browser treats opaquely, avoiding the DOM churn of traditional token-span highlighters. Worth a look for anyone building code-rendering UI where highlighting performance on large files matters. The link is the demo announcement, not a library.
